questions.q: In this lab's scenario, why is 'File' the correct Data Source type for the HR CSV?
options: JDBC would have been required instead, since sys_user is a database table
The Data Source type doesn't matter as long as a Transform Map exists
HR is providing a CSV file directly, not database or API access, so File matches how the source data is actually delivered
File is the only Data Source type ServiceNow supports
questions.explain: The Data Source type should match how the source system actually makes its data available — here, a CSV file.

questions.q: What happens to the 500 rows from new_hires_oct2026.csv immediately after the first load, before any Transform Map runs?
options: They land in an auto-created staging table like imp_new_hires, as a raw, unmodified copy with no validation yet
They are written directly into sys_user with full validation already applied
They are rejected because dept_name doesn't match the target field name exactly
They are silently discarded until a coalesce field is configured
questions.explain: Loading a Data Source only populates the staging table raw — mapping and validation happen later, in the Transform Map.

questions.q: Why does this scenario set the coalesce field to email rather than, say, first_name?
options: Coalesce fields must always be the first column in the staging table
first_name cannot be used in any Transform Map under any circumstances
Email happens to be the only field ServiceNow allows as a target field
Email is unique per person and stable across every month's file, making it a reliable match key for updates vs. inserts
questions.explain: A good coalesce field is unique and stable — first_name is neither, since many employees could share a first name.

questions.q: In November's run, why do the 500 returning employees update instead of creating 500 duplicate sys_user records?
options: Their email addresses match existing sys_user records, so coalesce triggers an update instead of an insert for each one
The Transform Map was rebuilt from scratch for the November file
The Scheduled Import blocks any row that appeared in a previous month's file
ServiceNow automatically detects duplicate names and merges them without any configuration
questions.explain: Coalesce on email finds an existing match for each returning employee and updates that record rather than inserting a new one.

questions.q: If coalesce had been left unset entirely, what would November's run have done per this lesson's reasoning?
options: Refused to run the import at all
Automatically picked email as the coalesce field by default
Updated all 540 rows correctly anyway, since dept_name was mapped as a reference lookup
Created 540 new duplicate sys_user records instead of correctly updating 500 and inserting 40
questions.explain: Without a coalesce field, the transform has no way to recognize existing records, so every row — new or returning — would simply insert.
